chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: The Kentucky Tavern Spook Breakfast and Kansas City musicians
summary: After-hours Spook Breakfasts brought together bands; Moore recalls Jay McShann, Baby Lovett, Nat Towles and Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh, yes, I always did solo work with the bands I was with. They would always put me in the show to play 'Stardust' or different solos that I did and when I was with Harlan, we were playing Fairland Park and my days in Kansas Tavern. City I had fond memories of the Kentucky Saturday night all the bands in the city would get finished and come to the Kentucky Tavern there and they called it the Spook Breakfast.
Spook Breakfast, yeh. Why did they call it that?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

I think it's because of all the spooks laying around, getting ready to have a ball by themselves, you know and all the famous bands would come to -- that's when I first met Charlie Parker. was Jay McShann The band was there in Kansas City as well as our band, Harlan Leonard, there was Tommy Douglas, clarinet player. He had a group there.

I met Baby Lovett there, he was playing at this club with -- I can't recall the name -- [Lee] Julia -- I can't recall her name, but she was famous, too and Baby Lovett was the greatest dresser, one guy I'll never forget because he always dressed -- light suits, light hat, beautiful shoes, he would stand in front of the poolroom there on the Cut, they called it the Cut, 18th and Vine. And then also I ran into Nat Toles from Omaha. Nat Toles band had Henry Coker, the trombonist. Buddy Tate was -- he served as an apprentice with Nat Toles, but he later came to be famous as he is now with the Count Basie band. Also along with Lester Young, Herschel Evans, that was one beautiful band. I had feelings to join that band, but I couldn't.
